summary: Inconsistent throttling (429) behavior across regions for same enterprise route; suspected policy/config propagation delay
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports inconsistent throttling behavior across regions for the same tenant + route. During a burst test, requests routed to us-east are receiving 429s (expected per configured per-route limit), while eu-west continues to accept traffic (unexpected) for ~8–15 minutes. Later the behavior flips (eu-west starts throttling, us-east relaxes), suggesting policy/config version drift.

Customer impact:
- Confusing and difficult to operate client-side retry/backoff logic (inconsistent behavior and Retry-After across regions).
- Risk of overload on the region not enforcing the intended protection policy.
- Customer is an enterprise account; they are using region-based failover and expect deterministic throttling semantics.

Environment:
- Production
- Regions: us-east, eu-west
- Route: /v1/chat/completions (enterprise hot route)
- Client uses two base URLs with weighted routing; sends same payload shape.

What the customer sees:
- us-east responses: HTTP 429 with Retry-After present; error body contains reason "over_capacity" / "rate_limit" (varies by region).
- eu-west responses: HTTP 200 during same timeframe, then later begins 429-ing.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Send sustained load at ~2x typical QPS for 10 minutes.
2) Route ~50% of traffic to us-east endpoint, ~50% to eu-west endpoint.
3) Observe 429 rate differs by region, inconsistent with expected per-route limit.

Support request:
- Confirm if per-route rate limits/quotas are regional or global.
- Identify why throttling enforcement differs between us-east and eu-west.
- Provide guidance on correct retry strategy until behavior is stable.

Attachments / references:
- Customer provided request IDs (sample): rwd_req_7f1c1f2b, rwd_req_7f1c203a, rwd_req_7f1c21e9
- Support internal thread: #support (ref: 1737689020)
- On-call coordination during capacity dip: #incidents (ref: 1737524410)
comments:
2025-01-28 (Dev Patel, Support) — Triage
Acknowledged customer report. Noted that in the hot-route capacity protection work, per-route rate limits are enforced at the gateway with policy pushed from the control plane; enforcement is expected to be consistent per-region within a few minutes. Asked customer to share: timestamps (UTC), which region base URL per request, and a few request IDs + response headers (Retry-After, request-id).

2025-01-28 (Northbridge Systems, Customer) — Repro details
Shared timestamps 17:05–17:22 UTC. us-east returned ~18% 429; eu-west 0% 429 for first ~12 minutes, then eu-west started returning 429 with different error payload formatting and Retry-After value. They confirmed same API key/tenant and same route. They are using a 2-region active/active config for resiliency and expected consistent throttling semantics.

2025-01-28 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Initial analysis / internal escalation
Pulled logs for sample request IDs. Observed different policy evaluation outcomes across regions for same tenant/route key. us-east gateway logs show policy_version=2025-01-28.3; eu-west shows policy_version=2025-01-28.1 for the impacted time window.
Hypothesis: policy engine config propagation lag or stale cache in eu-west.
Looped in Platform + SRE via #eng-oncall and tagged Rafael Mendes + Ethan Park.

Notes:
- This aligns with customer symptom: enforcement appears correct in one region and delayed in another.
- Not a runtime saturation-driven shed, appears to be config/version mismatch.

2025-01-28 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Investigation
Confirmed eu-west policy fetcher pods had increased watch lag (control-plane -> edge) during the same time window. The watch stream reconnect count spiked, and gateways continued to serve cached policy until refresh.
We do not currently expose policy version to the customer, making this hard to debug externally.
Immediate mitigation: forced restart of eu-west policy-cache sidecars and invalidated edge cache keys for the affected tenant/route. After restart, eu-west policy_version matched us-east and 429 rates aligned within ~2 minutes.

2025-01-29 (Ethan Park, Platform Control Plane) — Root cause summary
Root cause: config propagation delay due to intermittent watch disconnects in eu-west, combined with a long cache TTL on the gateway policy cache (10 minutes). When the watch was flapping, gateways relied on stale cached policy, causing region drift.

Contributing factors:
- Cache TTL tuned for stability under control plane outages, but too long for hot-route protection tuning.
- Missing regional SLI/alert for policy version divergence across regions.

Mitigations proposed:
1) Reduce TTL for hot-route protection policy to 60s (scoped to this policy family), keep other policy families at 10m.
2) Add metric + alert: policy_version_mismatch{region} for top N enterprise routes/tenants (cardinality-safe).
3) Add response header: X-Redwood-Policy-Version (debuggable; evaluate customer exposure/security impact).

2025-01-29 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Customer update
Shared findings with customer:
- Limits are enforced per-region at the gateway (not global). Under normal operation, policy changes propagate quickly; we identified a propagation lag in eu-west resulting in stale policy for ~10 minutes.
- We applied a mitigation (cache invalidation + restart) and confirmed consistent throttling behavior across us-east/eu-west.
- Recommended retry strategy until rollout completes: respect Retry-After header; use exponential backoff with jitter; cap retries; and avoid immediate region failover loops that amplify bursts.
Customer requested confirmation of permanent fix timeline and whether X-Redwood-Policy-Version will be available.

2025-02-01 (Sergio Costa, Observability) — Follow-up tracking
Created follow-up tasks under project umbrella ENG-4821:
- ENG-4827: add per-region policy propagation lag + mismatch dashboards/alerts (include links from #eng-oncall runbook)
- ENG-4828: rollout guardrails (block enabling new hot-route policies if propagation health degraded)
Also referenced cardinality review doc to ensure tenant/route labels are constrained to allowlisted hot routes only.

2025-02-02 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Resolution
Marked resolved after 72 hours without recurrence. eu-west policy propagation stable; throttling now consistent across regions for the affected route. Customer confirmed their burst test now yields aligned 429 rates and consistent Retry-After semantics.

Resolution details:
- Operational fix applied: eu-west policy cache invalidation + sidecar restart during incident window.
- Platform change queued: reduce TTL for hot-route protection policy cache (scoped change) + new mismatch alerting (tracked in ENG-4827/ENG-4828).

Customer-facing next steps:
- We will follow up once we decide on exposure of policy version header (likely behind enterprise debug flag).
- If customer sees recurrence, ask them to include request-id and region plus full response headers; we can correlate with policy_version logs.
resolution: Resolved. Root cause was regional policy/config propagation lag (watch disconnects) combined with long gateway cache TTL, causing stale hot-route protection policy in eu-west. Immediate mitigation: cache invalidation + policy sidecar restart in eu-west. Follow-ups tracked in Linear (ENG-4827 for dashboards/alerts; ENG-4828 for rollout guardrails; under umbrella ENG-4821).
